_meta.indication: LUZU (luliconazole) Cream, 1% is an azole antifungal indicated for the topical treatment of interdigital tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis caused by Trichophyton rubrum and Epidermophyton floccosum, in patients 18 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study; luliconazole cream 1% once daily for 14 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 12 years or older with clinical diagnosis of interdigital tinea pedis and positive KOH and fungal culture
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving complete clearance (clinical cure and mycological cure) at Day 42
pivotal_trials.result: Complete clearance 28/106 (26.4%) luliconazole vs 2/103 (1.9%) vehicle; treatment difference 24.5% (95% CI 15.5%, 34%); p<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study, identical in design to Study 02; luliconazole cream 1% once daily for 14 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 12 years or older with clinical diagnosis of interdigital tinea pedis and positive KOH and fungal culture
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving complete clearance (clinical cure and mycological cure) at Day 42
pivotal_trials.result: Complete clearance 15/107 (14.0%) luliconazole vs 3/107 (2.8%) vehicle; treatment difference 11.2% (95% CI 3.7%, 19.5%); p<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, vehicle-controlled study; luliconazole cream 1% once daily for 7 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 12 years or older with clinical diagnosis of tinea cruris
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving complete clearance (clinical cure and mycological cure) at Day 28
pivotal_trials.result: Complete clearance 35/165 (21.2%) luliconazole vs 4/91 (4.4%) vehicle; treatment difference 15.8% (95% CI 7.8%, 24.6%); p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were application site reactions, which occurred in less than 1% of subjects in both the LUZU and vehicle arms; most adverse reactions were mild in severity. Postmarketing reactions include contact dermatitis and cellulitis.
target_moa: Luliconazole is an azole (imidazole) antifungal that inhibits fungal ergosterol biosynthesis, a constituent of fungal cell membranes, via inhibition of the enzyme lanosterol 14α-demethylase.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the product presented no novel or complex scientific or regulatory issues requiring advisory committee discussion.

description.text: Expanded to a new (pediatric) patient population for Luzu (luliconazole) cream, 1%

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for a new patient population.

summary.text: Standard full approval of a new molecular entity (topical azole antifungal) via a 505(b) NDA, received December 11, 2012 and approved on the basis of three Phase 3 vehicle-controlled trials with no advisory committee; PREA pediatric studies were deferred/waived with required postmarketing studies.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received December 11, 2012, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for LUZU (luliconazole) Cream, 1%.
The application triggers PREA as luliconazole is a New Molecular Entity and thus a new active ingredient requiring a pediatric study plan.

Although luliconazole is a new molecular entity, it was determined that this new topical azole antifungal cream presented no novel or complex scientific or regulatory issues that required advisory committee discussion.
